messages:
Maria: Quick sync — we need to pick a prioritization approach for the Q2 pricing rollout. Do we do a full RICE score for each pricing feature (rate limits, tiers, reserved capacity, burst credits) or a simpler impact vs effort matrix? I sketched a sequencing idea: 1) baseline tiers + rate limits, 2) burst credits, 3) reserved offering. Thoughts? Meeting 11am PT.

Kevin: +1 on sequencing but fyi reserved brings nontrivial infra work (pooling, placement, billing hooks). If we do reserved before metering/billing hooks are solid we’ll have a lot of manual ops. :grimacing:

Devin: From sales — several customers are pushing for reserved capacity earlier. They care about predictability more than price per token. If we can show a small committed SKU (1-3 GPUs equivalent) that would close some deals.

Anya: Agree we should score. Proposal: R=estimated # affected customers in 6 months, I=expected uplift in conversion/retention (0.25/0.5/1/2x), C=confidence (data/back-of-envelope), E=engineering months. Quick sketch:
```
Feature                    R   I    C    E   RICE
baseline tiers + limits    8   1.0  0.8  1   64
burst credits              6   0.6  0.6  1   21.6
reserved capacity          4   1.5  0.6  3   12
flex commit (hybrid)       3   1.8  0.5  2   13.5
```
Numbers are rough but baseline tiers score highest.

Emily: From finance — reserved moves revenue forward (good) but adds recognition complexity + potential headroom mismatch. PAYG gives us cleaner metrics early and captures usage growth. Suggest we prioritize a solid PAYG tier + conservative rate-limits, then offer a simple reserved MVP with a 3-month commit window.

Kevin: Implementation order I’d recommend: 1) metering & rate-limit enforcement per API key, 2) billing events pipeline + pricing hooks, 3) UI/console for purchase + reservation, 4) backend pool/placement. That lets us ship tiers quickly while laying foundation for reserved. Example config keys we’ll need: 
```
rate_limit: {period: "minute", tokens: 1200}
quota_model: {window_days: 30, soft_threshold_pct: 85}
reserved_pool: {sku: "r4x.large", capacity_slots: 10}
```

Maria: Good call. Draft launch criteria for tiered rollout: 
- Tier definitions live in console + docs
- Rate limits enforced at 95% p95 latency under normal load
- Billing events show <1% loss and reconcile in sandbox
- Two pilot customers on PAYG; one customer trialing reserved MVP
- Monitor: conversion rate, churn, ARPA, 95th latency, overcommit events

Devin: I can line up two pilots: one fintech customer (needs strict SLAs) and one mid-market SaaS that cares about cost predictability. Prefer reserved pilot on the fintech if infra can provide an isolated pool.

Anya: We should define the A/B telemetry plan for measuring impact vs effort. Minimal plan: randomize new signups into 'baseline tier w/ conservative rate limits' vs 'baseline + burst credits' and measure 30-day retention + paid conversion. Also track per-customer token usage distribution pre/post.

pm-bot: doc created — https://drive.redwood/roadmaps/pricing/q2-pricing-playtest (PR: #1426) :rocket:

Emily: Sounds good. Voting thumbs: I support RICE to prioritize but sequence to deliver PAYG first, reserved as beta. Will check revenue recognition with accounting and add guardrails for early refunds. :thumbsup:

Maria: OK we’ll run with RICE + sequence above. Action items: Anya to finalize RICE scores by EOD, Kevin to draft implementation plan for metering & billing hooks, Devin to confirm pilot customers, Emily to validate revenue recognition constraints with accounting. Follow-up 11am.

Kevin: noted. I’ll add a short tech-risk column to the RICE doc (compat + SRE ops).

Devin: looping in legal for a simple MSA for reserved pilots.

Anya: will push updated spreadsheet in the doc and add confidence intervals.

Maria: thanks everyone — see you 11am.
